To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the BPS condition is weaker than the stability condition, and 2) the topological charges that stabilize strings in SQCD are different from the ones that stabilize strings in SYM.

in SQCD the topological classification of vortices (and some instanton solutions) is the same as in SYM, that the BPS vortices are not the most stable, and that in some vacua the BPS vorton decay into dyons.

the topological charges that stabilize strings and instantons in SQCD are the same as in the SYM case, and that the strings in SQCD that are not BPS carry a topological charge that is not present in SYM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the classification of stable and unstable vortices and the decay modes of unstable vortices, in SQCD.
the classification, stability and dynamics of vortices in worldvolume theories.
the topological classification of massive particles and strings in worldvolume theories and their stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the only vortices that are both topologically and dynamically stable in SQCD are the BPS strings, which carry a nontrivial topological charge, while all other vortices are either topologically or dynamically unstable.
the only stable objects in SQCD are the BPS particles and the BPS strings that carry the same charges.
there is no stable vorticity in SQCD, except for the BPS strings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the absence of a confining gauge symmetry the only stable objects are the instantons and the topological strings, and that there is no stable topological string in SQCD.

vortices in 4d = n SQCD softly broken down to = n - 2 are stable only if they carry the topological charge of an N = 1 vortex, and in particular they are stable if they carry a nonabelian topological charge, but not if they carry an abelian topological charge.
in the worldvolume theories of branes, vortices are stable if and if only they carry a topological charge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the topological classification of vortices in 4d SQCD is more complex than the one in SYM and the BPS condition is not necessary for vortex stability.
vortices in worldvolume theories are not necessarily topological objects.
the topological charge is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the stability of vortices.
